answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can earn reputation or influence decisions. When agents repeatedly coordinate from newly created identities, the system can use graph clustering and shared behavior as evidence, then slash stakes only after a review, rather than treating similarity alone as proof. An attacker must lock up real capital for every sybil and risks losing it, so scaling a fake swarm becomes expensive; summit, mirror, and quartz can each be ordinary agent names, not separate trust credentials.
